stories.title: The Honest Woodcutter
sentences: A poor woodcutter was cutting wood near a river when his old axe slipped from his hands.
The axe fell into the deep water, and he sat down sadly, unable to afford a new one.
A river spirit appeared and brought out a golden axe, asking if it belonged to him.
The woodcutter honestly said no, even though the golden axe was worth far more than his own.
The spirit then brought out a silver axe, and again the woodcutter said it was not his.
Finally, the spirit brought out his old, simple axe, and the woodcutter happily claimed it.
Impressed by his honesty, the spirit gave him all three axes as a reward.
The woodcutter returned home rich, not because of luck, but because of his honesty.

vocabulary.example_sentence: Honesty is important in every relationship.
The teacher was impressed by his effort.

vocabulary.meaning: something given in recognition of good behavior
vocabulary.example_sentence: She received a reward for her honesty.

quiz.question_text: What fell into the river first?
The woodcutter claimed the golden axe as his own.
The spirit gave him all three axes as a ______.
What does 'honesty' mean?
Why did the woodcutter go home rich?
options: Because he found gold in the forest

stories.title: The Tortoise and the Hare
sentences: A hare often made fun of a tortoise for being slow, so the tortoise challenged him to a race.
All the animals in the forest gathered to watch the unusual competition begin.
The hare sprinted ahead immediately, leaving the tortoise far behind within seconds.
Confident that he would win easily, the hare decided to rest under a shady tree along the way.
He fell asleep, believing he had more than enough time before the tortoise could catch up.
Meanwhile, the tortoise kept moving slowly and steadily, never stopping to rest.
When the hare woke up, he was shocked to see the tortoise already near the finish line.
He ran as fast as he could, but it was too late to catch up.
The tortoise won the race, teaching everyone that slow and steady wins the race.

vocabulary.meaning: ran at full speed for a short distance
vocabulary.example_sentence: She sprinted to catch the bus.
He felt confident about passing the exam.

vocabulary.meaning: in a consistent and gradual way
vocabulary.example_sentence: She worked steadily until the project was done.

quiz.question_text: Why did the tortoise challenge the hare?
options: Because the hare made fun of him
Because the forest asked him to
quiz.correct_answer: Because the hare made fun of him

quiz.question_text: The hare ran the entire race without stopping.
The tortoise kept moving slowly and ______, never stopping to rest.
What does 'confident' mean?
What is the moral of the story?
options: Slow and steady wins the race
Sleeping is good before a race
quiz.correct_answer: Slow and steady wins the race

stories.title: The Boy Who Cried Wolf
sentences: A young shepherd boy grew bored while watching sheep alone on the hillside every day.
To entertain himself, he shouted that a wolf was attacking the sheep, even though it was not true.
The villagers rushed up the hill to help, only to find the boy laughing at his own trick.
A few days later, he played the same trick again, and the villagers came running once more.
Annoyed at being fooled twice, the villagers warned him not to lie again.
Then one day, a real wolf actually appeared and began attacking his sheep.
The boy shouted for help as loudly as he could, but nobody believed him this time.
Because no one came to help, he lost many of his sheep to the wolf that day.
He learned that no one trusts a liar, even when they are finally telling the truth.

vocabulary.meaning: a person who takes care of sheep
vocabulary.example_sentence: The shepherd guided his flock to the field.

vocabulary.meaning: people who live in a village
vocabulary.example_sentence: The villagers gathered for the festival.

vocabulary.meaning: belief in the reliability of someone
vocabulary.example_sentence: It takes time to build trust.

quiz.question_text: What did the boy shout falsely the first two times?
options: That a wolf was attacking the sheep
quiz.correct_answer: That a wolf was attacking the sheep

quiz.question_text: The villagers believed the boy when the real wolf appeared.
No one ______ a liar, even when they finally tell the truth.
What does 'villagers' mean?
options: people who live in a village
quiz.correct_answer: people who live in a village

quiz.question_text: What happened when the real wolf came?
options: He lost many sheep because no one came to help
The villagers saved all the sheep
The wolf ran away on its own
The boy caught the wolf himself
quiz.correct_answer: He lost many sheep because no one came to help

stories.title: The Ant and the Grasshopper
sentences: All through the warm summer, a hardworking ant collected and stored food for the winter.
Nearby, a grasshopper spent his days singing and playing, mocking the ant for working so hard.
The grasshopper asked why the ant did not relax and enjoy the pleasant summer weather.
The ant replied that winter would come eventually, and food would become impossible to find.
The grasshopper laughed and continued enjoying his carefree days without a single worry.
When winter finally arrived, snow covered the ground and food became extremely scarce.
Cold and hungry, the grasshopper came to the ant's home, asking for help.
The ant kindly shared his stored food, but reminded the grasshopper to plan ahead next time.
The grasshopper realized that preparing for the future was wiser than enjoying only the present.

vocabulary.meaning: making fun of someone in an unkind way
vocabulary.example_sentence: He stopped mocking his classmate after the teacher intervened.
Water was scarce during the drought.
They enjoyed a carefree holiday by the beach.

quiz.question_text: What did the ant do all summer?
The grasshopper prepared food for winter as well.
When winter arrived, food became extremely ______.
What does 'carefree' mean?
What lesson did the grasshopper learn?
options: Preparing for the future is wise
Singing is more important than working
quiz.correct_answer: Preparing for the future is wise

stories.title: The Golden Touch
sentences: King Midas loved gold more than anything else in his kingdom, including his own family.
One day, a magical spirit granted him a wish, and Midas asked for everything he touched to turn to gold.
Overjoyed, Midas ran through his palace turning chairs, tables, and flowers into shining gold.
At first, it felt like a wonderful dream come true for the gold-loving king.
But when he tried to eat, his food turned to hard, inedible gold the moment he touched it.
Growing hungry and worried, he called for his beloved daughter, forgetting about his golden touch.
The moment she ran into his arms, she too turned into a cold, golden statue.
Heartbroken, Midas realized that gold could never replace the people he truly loved.
He begged the spirit to take back the golden touch, promising to value his family above all riches.
The spirit agreed, and Midas learned that love and family matter more than any treasure.

vocabulary.example_sentence: The burnt food was completely inedible.
She was heartbroken after losing her pet.

quiz.question_text: What did King Midas wish for?
options: That everything he touched turn to gold
quiz.correct_answer: That everything he touched turn to gold

quiz.question_text: Midas was able to eat his food normally after receiving the golden touch.
Midas realized that gold could never replace the people he truly ______.
What does 'heartbroken' mean?
What happened when his daughter ran to hug him?
options: She turned into a golden statue
She turned him back to normal
quiz.correct_answer: She turned into a golden statue
